blocks.x: Las Vegas can be a disorienting place to visit. Over 85,000 hotel rooms crammed into a single corridor. A reputation for nickel-and-diming. Extreme heat. And far too many escalators.

But the city’s unique mythology—bright lights and round-the-clock entertainment for 55-year-olds and 5-year-olds alike—keeps people coming back. And despite the city’s incessant need to modernize and reinvent itself, it remains the larger-than-life, slightly flamboyant entertainment capital it was back in the 1950s, when crowds first took notice of the strange casino town in the middle of the desert.
“Old movies like Casino gave Vegas cachet,” says Juyoung Kang, who has helmed mixology programs on and off the Strip since the early 2000s. “You don’t find that character anywhere else.”

Kang, who currently oversees the bar program at Doberman Drawing Room, has lived and worked in Vegas for years. But she says she never fell out of love with what makes Vegas classic. “I’ve been to Caesars Palace so many times,” she says, “and somehow I still get excited seeing all the statues and the fountains."

That sense of discovery, she argues, has kept Vegas fresh, and it pushes people to continue to seek out new and unexpected pockets of the city. Yes, the casinos are designed to confuse you. And you’ll almost definitely get a little lost. But that’s actually the point.
Below, find a few ideas on how to make the most of your next Vegas trip.

Don’t sleep on the Italian food

Speaking of food, Vegas’s legacy of classic Italian-American dining goes all the way back to the Rat Pack days. Many of the old-school spots are still around, and they’re all fantastic. The Italian American Club, an off-Strip eatery with a dedicated lounge singer, is as charming as it is delicious. Meanwhile, Piero’s holds the title for best veal parm in Vegas (if you don’t believe us, ask Joe Pesci, who filmed multiple scenes from Casino right inside the restaurant).

Between the ungodly traffic, queueing for the elevator, and the wilting heat, seemingly small distances can take a while to cover in Vegas. You may think you’re only hopping across the street, or three casinos over, but it’s usually more complicated than that—particularly if you’re relying on rideshare services like Uber or Lyft. So leave more transit time than you think.
